q01,1,1,,multi,How long do eggs last in the fridge?,Fresh eggs in the shell: 3-5 weeks in the fridge (FDA storage chart); the FDA egg page says use them within 3 weeks for best quality.,"According to FDA guidance, fresh eggs in the shell should be stored promptly in a clean refrigerator at 40° F or below in their original carton and used within 3 weeks for best quality [fda:what-you-need-know-about-egg-safety
Storage times for other egg products in the refrigerator include:
* **Fresh, in shell:** 3 - 5 weeks [fda_storage_chart
* **Raw yolks, whites:** 2 - 4 days [fda_storage_chart
* **Hard cooked:** 1 week [fda_storage_chart
* **Liquid pasteurized eggs or egg substitutes:** 3 days if opened, or 10 days if unopened [fda_storage_chart
* **Leftover cooked egg dishes:** 3 to 4 days [fda:what-you-need-know-about-egg-safety

q03,1,1,,single,My pesto is past its date but I kept it frozen. Can I still eat it?,"Pesto is not listed, but the chart says food kept frozen at 0°F stays safe indefinitely; freezer times and dates are about quality, not safety.","Yes, you can still eat it. Product date labels (such as ""expires on,"" ""sell by,"" or ""best by"") indicate quality and flavor rather than safety [fda:how-cut-food-waste-and-maintain-food-safety]. Because freezing at 0° F (-18° C) keeps food safe indefinitely, the recommended freezer storage times are for quality only [fda_storage_chart
When you are ready to use the pesto, examine it for signs of spoilage and check if it has changed noticeably in color, consistency, or texture [fda:how-cut-food-waste-and-maintain-food-safety]."

q04,1,1,,single,How long does chicken last if I freeze it?,"Raw chicken: whole 1 year, parts 9 months (quality; frozen food stays safe indefinitely).","According to FDA guidelines, because freezing at 0°F (-18°C) keeps food safe indefinitely, recommended freezer storage times are for quality rather than safety [fda_storage_chart
For chicken in the freezer:
* **Whole chicken or turkey:** 1 year [fda_storage_chart
* **Chicken or turkey parts:** 9 months [fda_storage_chart
* **Giblets:** 3–4 months [fda_storage_chart
* **Fried chicken:** 4 months [fda_storage_chart
* **Cooked poultry dishes:** 4–6 months [fda_storage_chart
* **Chicken pieces (plain):** 4 months [fda_storage_chart
* **Chicken pieces covered with broth or gravy:** 6 months [fda_storage_chart
* **Chicken nuggets and patties:** 1–3 months [fda_storage_chart

Additionally, if you are freezing meat and poultry in its original package for longer than 2 months, the FDA recommends overwrapping the package with airtight heavy-duty foil, plastic wrap, or freezer paper, or placing it inside a plastic bag [fda_storage_chart

q05,1,1,,single,How long does meat last if I freeze it?,"Raw beef/pork: steaks 6-12 months, chops 4-6 months, roasts 4-12 months; hamburger/ground meat 3-4 months.","Because freezing at 0°F (-18°C) keeps food safe indefinitely, the recommended freezer storage times are for quality only [fda_storage_chart
According to the FDA's Refrigerator & Freezer Storage Chart, recommended freezer times for quality include:
* **Fresh Meat (Beef, Veal, Lamb, & Pork):**
* Steaks: 6–12 months [fda_storage_chart
* Chops: 4–6 months [fda_storage_chart
* Roasts: 4–12 months [fda_storage_chart
* **Raw Hamburger, Ground & Stew Meat:**
* Hamburger & stew meats: 3–4 months [fda_storage_chart
* Ground turkey, veal, pork, lamb: 3–4 months [fda_storage_chart
* **Fresh Poultry:**
* Chicken or turkey, whole: 1 year [fda_storage_chart
* Chicken or turkey, parts: 9 months [fda_storage_chart
* Giblets: 3–4 months [fda_storage_chart
* **Bacon & Sausage:**
* Bacon: 1 month [fda_storage_chart
* Sausage, raw from pork, beef, chicken, or turkey: 1–2 months [fda_storage_chart
* Smoked breakfast links, patties: 1–2 months [fda_storage_chart
* **Meat Leftovers:**
* Cooked meat & meat dishes: 2–3 months [fda_storage_chart
* Gravy & meat broth: 2–3 months [fda_storage_chart

If you are freezing meat and poultry in its original package for longer than 2 months, overwrap these packages with airtight heavy-duty foil, plastic wrap, or freezer paper; or place the package inside a plastic bag [fda_storage_chart

q14,1,1,,multi,How many days does salmon last in the fridge before I have to freeze it?,"1-2 days (fatty fish, storage chart); the seafood page says refrigerate only if used within 2 days, otherwise freeze.","Fresh fatty fish, such as salmon, can be stored in the refrigerator for **1 to 2 days** before you need to cook or freeze it [fda_storage_chart

q15,1,1,,multi,How many days does tuna last in the fridge before I have to freeze it?,"1-2 days (fish, storage chart); refrigerate only if used within 2 days, otherwise freeze.","According to FDA storage guidelines, the length of time fresh tuna (classified as a fatty fish) lasts in the refrigerator depends on whether it is fresh or prepared:
* **Fresh fatty fish (like tuna):** 1 to 2 days in the refrigerator before you need to freeze or cook it [fda_storage_chart
* **Cooked fish:** 3 to 4 days in the refrigerator [fda_storage_chart
* **Tuna salad (store-prepared or homemade):** 3 to 5 days in the refrigerator (do not freeze) [fda_storage_chart
* **Opened canned seafood out of the can:** 3 to 4 days in the refrigerator [fda_storage_chart

q17,1,1,,single,Do I need to keep my protein in a tupperware in the fridge?,"Yes: store refrigerated foods in covered containers or sealed storage bags, and check leftovers daily for spoilage.","Whether you need to keep your protein in a Tupperware container depends on whether it is raw or cooked:
* **Raw Meat and Poultry:** The FDA recommends keeping fresh meat and poultry in its original package until just before using [fda_storage_chart

* **Cooked Protein / Leftovers:** If you have cooked meat, poultry, or other prepared protein dishes, they should be refrigerated within 2 hours of cooking [fda:refrigerator-thermometers-cold-facts-about-food-safety
column2: Section: Quick Chill; Thaw with Care]. To help hot food cool faster, the FDA recommends dividing leftovers into smaller containers (such as Tupperware) before placing them in the refrigerator [fda:refrigerator-thermometers-cold-facts-about-food-safety
column3: Section: Quick Chill; Thaw with Care]."

q19,1,1,,multi,What is botulism?,"A disease caused by a deadly toxin made by the bacterium Clostridium botulinum, characterised by muscle paralysis.","Botulism is a serious, sometimes fatal disease caused by a potent neurotoxin formed during the growth of *Clostridium botulinum* [bad_bug_book
column2: p. 108, Clostridium botulinum > 2. Disease]. The infection results in flaccid paralysis of muscles, including those of the respiratory tract [bad_bug_book

column1: ### Types and Causes

* **Foodborne Botulism:** A severe type of food poisoning caused by ingesting foods containing the toxin produced by *C. botulinum*, most often developing after consumption of improperly processed and inadequately cooked home-preserved foods [bad_bug_book
* **Infant Botulism:** A serious illness caused by the ingestion of *C. botulinum* spores that colonize and produce toxin in the intestinal tracts of infants [bad_bug_book
column2: p. 108, Clostridium botulinum > 2. Disease (part 2)]. Honey is a known dietary reservoir of these spores and should never be fed to children under 1 year of age [bad_bug_book
column3: p. 111, Clostridium botulinum > 3. Frequency; 4. Sources; 5. Target Populations; 6. Diagnosis].

column1: * **Wound Botulism:** The rarest form of botulism, which results when *C. botulinum* colonizes in a wound and produces toxins that reach other parts of the body via the bloodstream; this form is not foodborne [bad_bug_book
### Symptoms

* **Adult / Foodborne Symptoms:** Early symptoms typically start 18 to 36 hours after ingesting food containing the toxin (though times can vary from 4 hours to 8 days) and include double or blurred vision, drooping eyelids, slurred speech, difficulty swallowing, dry mouth, and muscle weakness [bad_bug_book
column2: p. 108, Clostridium botulinum > 2. Disease (part 4)]. If left untreated, symptoms may progress to paralysis of the arms, legs, trunk, and respiratory muscles [bad_bug_book

column1: * **Infant Symptoms:** Constipation after a period of normal development is often the first sign, followed by a flat facial expression, poor feeding (weak sucking), weak cry, decreased movement, trouble swallowing with excessive drooling, muscle weakness, and breathing problems [bad_bug_book

column1: q22,1,1,,multi,"If I thaw chicken, can I freeze it again?",Food that still has ice crystals or is at 40°F or below can be refrozen; food that thawed and was refrozen gives bacteria a chance to grow.,"Whether you can refreeze chicken after thawing depends on how it was thawed and kept:
* If the chicken was thawed **in the refrigerator**, it can be safely refrozen without cooking.
* If the chicken was thawed **in cold water or in the microwave**, it must be cooked immediately and should not be refrozen raw [fda:refrigerator-thermometers-cold-facts-about-food-safety
column2: Section: Safe Food Handling: Four Simple Steps (part 2)].

column1: * If the chicken was ever left to thaw at room temperature or left unrefrigerated, it is unsafe and should be thrown out [fda:refrigerator-thermometers-cold-facts-about-food-safety
column2: Section: Quick Chill; Thaw with Care]."
